title: Counting only the ones that match
idea: A counter can count only passes where a simple condition is true (count how many).

exercises.prompt: We want to count how many numbers from 1 to 5 are greater than 3. What will the counter hold?
exercises.explanation: Only 4 and 5 are greater than 3, so the counter should end at 2.
i is 1..5; only 4 and 5 pass i > 3, so the counter is raised twice and prints 2.

exercises.prompt: In that loop, on which passes does count go up?
exercises.explanation: Only when i > 3 — that is i = 4 and i = 5. On other passes the counter is untouched.

exercises.prompt: When the condition is false, the counter stays the same on that pass.
exercises.explanation: True. The += 1 line only runs when the if is true, so a false pass leaves the count unchanged.

exercises.prompt: How many numbers from 1 to 6 are even? (even means i % 2 == 0)
exercises.explanation: 2, 4, 6 are even — three of them. A counter with if i % 2 == 0 would end at 3.

exercises.prompt: Arrange a loop that counts how many numbers 1..5 are even.
exercises.explanation: Start counter at 0, loop, if even add 1, then print the count.
Less-than is <. Numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 are below 5, so the counter ends at 4.
i = 1, 2, 3, 4 are below 5 — four matches — so the counter prints 4.

exercises.prompt: If NONE of the numbers match the condition, what does the counter hold?
exercises.explanation: No matches means no +1 ever runs, so the counter keeps its start value, 0.

exercises.prompt: Why keep the counter start (count = 0) outside the if as well as outside the loop?
options: So it is ready once before any counting
exercises.explanation: It must be set once before counting begins; placing it inside the if would reset it on matches.
